incident-bot: [PAGER] High 5xx + websocket disconnects for tenant=helios-prod in us-west-2-dedicated-9; streaming error rate 18% over 6m, connection churn rising. Paging oncall @Maya. https://redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-1779002222 :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): ack. grabbing logs and curl checks. Sam, any customer notes?
Sam (support): Helios-ops reports intermittent 502/504 from our VPC gateway. Their mobile clients show repeated reconnects, creating a cascade. They say it started ~09:40 PDT. They've paused new deploys.
Lucas (platform): looking at edge proxies 10: lots of short lived TCP sessions ending with `ws: close 1006` and upstream `context deadline exceeded`. Also a visible jump in `accepts/sec` and `auth failures` remain normal. Pool metrics show worker RSS increase and stream queue latency rising.
Priya (eng-runtime): KV cache churn on stream shards for that pool. Eviction rate spiked 8x at 09:38. We see many concurrent `init_stream` calls for same session prefixes. Hypothesis: client reconnect storm -> cache thrash -> backend processing stalls -> timeouts.
Maya (oncall): what's the pool commit state? Can we add capacity?
Lucas (platform): dedicated-9 is at commit cap, autoscaler disabled by policy. We can do a temporary ephemeral pool in same AZ (helios-ephemeral-01) but must throttle its resource allocation to avoid stealing others' reserved capacity. I can carve out ephemeral spare if allowed.
Ava (acct): flagged to Helios that were investigating. Theyre concerned about patient-facing downtime. They authorize short-term routing to an isolate pool and request we minimize cross-tenant impact.
Helios-ops (customer): confirm we can change client reconnect behavior if you perform server-side throttling. We'll implement 5s backoff immediately.
Maya (oncall): immediate mitigations proposal (minimal blast radius):
- Add a per-tenant token-bucket limiter at gateway ingress: burst=200, rate=30/s.
- Set stream_idle_timeout=90s for helios-prod.
- Disable automatic per-request retries for this tenant (squelch at gateway).
- If above fails, shift traffic to `helios-ephemeral-01` with strict conn caps.
Commands (runbook extract):
```
# add per-tenant limiter
rb gw policy update --tenant helios-prod --add ingress_rate_limit "burst=200,rate=30/s"
# disable gateway retries for tenant
rb gw policy update --tenant helios-prod --set retry_on_5xx=false
# create ephemeral pool (low priority/low cap)
rb pools create helios-ephemeral-01 --region us-west-2 --type streaming --workers 2 --conn_limit 1200 --reason "incident mitigation"
rb route update helios-prod --target-pool helios-ephemeral-01 --grace 15s
```
Lucas (platform): applied ingress limiter and disabled retries. Observed `ingress_throttle` counters rising for helios-prod immediately (expected).
Priya (eng-runtime): after throttle, stream churn dropped ~45% in 90s; eviction rate halved. Error rate fell from 18% -> 7% in first 3min. KV cache hit-rate started to recover.
Sam (support): Helios confirms mobile reconnects slowed down after implementing 5s backoff; user-visible errors dropping. They still see occasional long tails for previously-stalled sessions.
Maya (oncall): good. Lucas, prepare ephemeral pool in case we need it. Do not route unless Helios consents or we hit threshold (error_rate >12% for 5m).
Lucas (platform): creating `helios-ephemeral-01` now with strict caps (conn_limit 1200, per_client_rate_limit 40/s). Health checks green. Not routing yet.
Priya (eng-runtime): can we add a temporary circuit-breaker at app-proxy layer: fail-fast for connections that exceed 3 retries in 60s to avoid long lived stuck loops? That buys time and reduces cache pressure.
Maya (oncall): yes, enable circuit-breaker for tenant (soft-fail).
Commands:
```
# enable circuit-breaker
rb gw policy update --tenant helios-prod --set circuit_breaker="retries=3,window=60s,action=failfast"
```
Lucas (platform): deployed circuit-breaker. Metrics show fewer long-running tasks and CPU consumption per-worker lowered ~20%.
Ava (acct): scheduled follow-up call with Helios for 10:30 PDT to review long-term fixes (backoff guidance, client heartbeat recommendations, resilience patterns).
Maya (oncall): logging actions to INC-20260315-0112 and will monitor. Ben, can you take watch after me?
Ben (oncall-next): taking handoff at 11:00 PDT. I'll monitor `helios-prod` and `helios-ephemeral-01`. Page if error_rate>10% or sustained eviction spikes.
OpsBot: runbook step `vpc-gw-per-tenant-rate-limit` executed by Maya.
Priya (eng-runtime): follow-ups for postmortem:
- Investigate KV cache eviction policy under reconnect storms; consider graceful degradation (prefetch+early-ack) for streaming init.
- Add alert automation: when tenant 5xx >12% and pool at commit capacity -> suggest isolation and allow one-click create ephemeral pool.
- Evaluate exposing per-tenant throttle metrics to customers via console.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. Current status: throttling + circuit-breaker active, error rate stabilized ~6-8%, no cross-tenant anomalies detected. Holding incident open for monitoring 60m.
Helios-ops (customer): thanks for fast response. We'll attend the 10:30 follow-up.
Maya (oncall): handing to Ben in 45m. If any regression, page PD pager. :white_check_mark:
Ben (oncall-next): ack 1: I'll be on watch.
Maya (oncall): closing the pager for now, leaving incident open for postmortem items and customer follow-up.
